seg_001: You can recognise it by its height, 25.5 metres, tall enough to read against the stone from a street away. It stands in the Plaza de la Merced, just below the cathedral.
seg_002: You can recognise it by the lightning conductor fitted after a 1991 strike, standing beside its companion tree in front of the collegiate church. It stands on the Alameda del Medio Punto, La Granja.
seg_003: You can recognise it by standing over the fountain of Perseus and the sea monster, the second-tallest sequoia in these gardens. It stands in the Parterre de Andromeda, La Granja.
seg_004: You can recognise it as the tallest tree here that is not a sequoia, 36.5 metres, standing beside the dragon fountain. It stands at the Fuente de los Dragones, La Granja.
seg_005: You can recognise it by needles standing out in every direction like a bottle brush, and cones that disintegrate on the tree rather than falling whole. It stands in the Parterre del Potosi, La Granja.
seg_006: You can recognise it by its flat, tiered branches spreading out horizontally in layers, beside the sequoia in the same parterre. It stands in the Parterre de Andromeda, La Granja.
